issues.item: Triggers: Sexual Trauma Cues: Comments on sexual violence
issues.explanation: For a terrorism trauma, sexual-violence comments as a primary trigger is hard to reconcile unless the index event also involved sexual assault or closely related content; nothing else in the profile supports that connection.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Betrayal: I was betrayed by someone I trusted
issues.explanation: The appraisal of betrayal by a trusted person is difficult to fit with terrorism as the trauma type unless there was a clear interpersonal betrayal component; the rest of the selected items describe loss of control, helplessness, avoidance, dissociation, and substance use rather than interpersonal betrayal.

vignette: Vikram Sharma was thirty-two when the coordinated terrorist attack at the central transit hub turned a routine Tuesday commute into a sudden collapse of order. He had been standing near a security checkpoint when the first explosion threw him backward against the tiled wall, followed by a rapid staccato of gunfire as officers moved through the smoking concourse. What stayed with him was not the graze on his forearm, but the sharp, metallic crack of bullets striking the metal railings and the utter loss of control as the crowd surged, pressing him forward without choice. He had come to believe that once the first thing broke, everything else would follow, and he could not stop the cascade. The attack made the gunshot noise potent; it was not merely loud, but distinctly rhythmic and sudden, mirroring the strike itself. He began waking in the dark, his body rigid beneath the sheets, certain that the sudden snap of a house pipe or the low hum of the refrigerator was a prelude to impact. The world, which he had always treated as navigable, now felt fundamentally dangerous, a place where violence could arrive without warning. As months accumulated, Vikram’s professional habits quietly shifted into protective routines. He continued to work as a psychologist at a metropolitan clinic, but his daily environment became a landscape of potential stressors. He started declining late consultations, cancelling evening seminars, and leaving early on days when deadlines clustered. He was certain that adding another demand would tip the balance again. When pressure mounted in his office, surrounded by the familiar hum of electronic doorbells and the rustle of patient files, he would simply drift off into a world of his own, focusing on the grain of his wooden desk or the steady rhythm of his breathing until the moment passed. At night, the dark grew heavy, and he found himself drinking a glass of whiskey or taking his prescribed medication before sleep, not because of a prescription, but for the relief the substances provided. His wife, Priya, noticed the changes first; the man who once packed for spontaneous trips now measured everything, who once spoke in broad, confident tones now often answered in short, deliberate phrases. He was not broken, but he was unrecognisable to himself. The person he had become moved carefully through days, checking exits, timing his movements, and keeping his emotions banked. Now thirty-seven, Vikram sits in his clinic office during a quiet afternoon, the late afternoon light slicing through the blinds. A PCL-5 score of sixty-nine sits on his chart, but the number only partly captures the weight he carries. He has come to see help not as a surrender to weakness, but as a recalibration of the lens through which he views threat. What finally brought him to schedule this intake was a Tuesday morning when a colleague’s dropped metal clipboard produced a sharp clatter that sent him to the floor, knees buckling, heart racing, before he could even stand. It was then that he recognized the unrecognisable self staring back from the glass partition. He is most afraid of the sudden loss of control, of being caught unguarded again when the world turns violent. He hopes, more than anything, that the person he was before the hub can be found again, not by erasing the fear, but by learning to carry it without letting it dictate every breath, every sound, and every quiet night.
